sanskrit: doṣo gāya bṛhad gāya dyumad gāyātharvaṇa | stuhi devaṃ savitāram ||
english: Sing at evening, sing the great hymn, sing it brilliantly, O Atharvan. Praise the god Savitṛ.

sanskrit: tam u stuhy antaḥsindhuṃ sūnuṃ satyasya yuvānam | adroghavācaṃ suśevam ||
english: Praise him, the one within the river, the son of truth, the youthful one — he of guileless speech, of goodly grace.

sanskrit: sa ghā no devaḥ savitā- -āsāviṣad vasupatir vasūni | ubhe suṣṭutī sugātum ||
english: May that god Savitṛ, lord of good things, press out for us good things — through this good praise may he grant us easy passage.

sanskrit: indrāya somam ṛtvijaḥ sunotanā ca dhāvata | stotur yo havaṃ śṛṇavad dhavaṃ ca naḥ ||
english: O priests, press the soma for Indra and run the rite — he who hears the praiser's call, and hears our invocation.

sanskrit: sunotā somapāvne somam indrāya vajriṇe | yuvā jeteśānaḥ sa puruṣṭutaḥ ||
english: Press the soma for Indra the soma-drinker, the wielder of the vajra — he is the young conqueror, the ruler, much praised by men.

sanskrit: ā tvā viśantv indavo vayo na vṛkṣam andhasaḥ | virapśin vi mṛdho jahi rakṣasvinīḥ ||
english: Let the soma drops enter you, O full one, as birds enter a tree — crush and strike down the hostile demons.

sanskrit: āre asāv asmad astu hetir devāso asat | āre martānām aśastiḥ ||
english: Far from us be that bolt, O gods — may it be elsewhere. Far from mortals be the curse.

sanskrit: sakhaiva no rātir astu sakhendraḥ sakhā savitā | sakhā bhagaḥ satyadharmā no astu ||
english: May our bounty be as a friend; may Indra be our friend, and Savitṛ our friend. May Bhaga, of true law, be our friend.

sanskrit: abhi no devīr avasā mahāśarmaṇā nṛpatnīḥ | acchinnapatrāḥ sacantām ||
english: May the divine goddesses, mistresses of men, attend us with great shelter and aid — they whose wings are uncut.

sanskrit: īḍe agniṃ bhavaṃ sarvaṃ rakṣa ubjad ahiṃ balāsam uta sedim ugrām | āre asmad adite daivyaṃ bhayaṃ suvīryaṃ marutaḥ śarma yacchata ||
english: I implore Agni and Bhava — all protect us, press down the serpent, the disease, and fierce plague. O Aditi, keep divine fear far from us; O Maruts, grant us shelter and heroic strength.

sanskrit: īḍe dyāvāpṛthivī parvatām̐ apaḥ svaḥ sūryam urv antarikṣam | vanaspatīn oṣadhīr gā uta rca ṛtasya naḥ patayo mṛḍayantu ||
english: I implore heaven and earth, the mountains, the waters, the sky, the sun, the broad atmosphere, the forest trees, the plants, the cows, and the sacred verses — may the lords of cosmic order be gracious to us.

sanskrit: huve viṣṇuṃ pūṣaṇaṃ brahmaṇaspatiṃ bhagaṃ nu śaṃsaṃ savitāram ūtaye | iha somo varuṇo vāyur agnir bhaga ugrā avase no gamantu ||
english: I call Viṣṇu, Pūṣan, Brahmaṇaspati, Bhaga, the worthy Savitṛ for our aid. May Soma, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Agni, and mighty Bhaga come here to protect us.

sanskrit: pātaṃ na indrāpūṣaṇā varuṇaḥ pāntu marutaḥ | apāṃ napāt sindhavaḥ sapta pātana pātu viṣṇur uta dyauḥ ||
english: May Indra and Pūṣan protect us; may Varuṇa and the Maruts protect us. O Child of the Waters, O seven rivers, protect us — may Viṣṇu protect us, and heaven too.

sanskrit: pātāṃ no dyāvāpṛthivī abhiṣṭaye pātu grāvā pātu somo no aṃhasaḥ | pātu no devī suhavā sarasvatī pātv agnir ye śivā asya pāyavaḥ ||
english: May heaven and earth protect us for our victory; may the pressing stone protect us, may Soma protect us from distress. May the goddess Sarasvatī, of sweet invocation, protect us; may Agni protect us with his benevolent guardians.

sanskrit: pātāṃ no devāśvinā sudaṃsasā- -uṣāsānaktota na uruṣyatām | apāṃ napād avihrutī kayasya cid devo mūrdhann adite śarma yaccha naḥ ||
english: May the two divine Aśvins, of great wonders, protect us; may Dawn and Night keep us safe. O Child of the Waters, of unwavering protection — O god at the summit of all — O Aditi, grant us shelter.

sanskrit: tvaṣṭā me daivyaṃ vacaḥ parjanyo brahmaṇaspatiḥ | putrair bhrātṛbhir aditir nu pātu no duṣṭaraṃ trāmaṇe śavaḥ ||
english: Tvaṣṭṛ, my divine speech, Parjanya, Brahmaṇaspati — may Aditi now protect us with sons and brothers; may she grant strength hard to cross for our rescue.

sanskrit: aṃśo bhago varuṇo mitro aryamā- -aditiḥ pātv aṃhasaḥ | apa tasya dveṣo gamed avihruto yāvayāc chatrum ?anti tam? ||
english: May Aṃśa, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, and Aditi protect us from distress. May the unharmed one drive away his enmity, and ward off the enemy near him.

sanskrit: deva tvaṣṭar vardhaya sarvatātaye dhiye sam u śriye prāvatān naḥ | uruṣyā ṇa urutarāprayucchan dyauṣ pitar yāvaya ducchunām itaḥ ||
english: O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, increase us for all wholeness; advance our resolve and our glory together. Protect us, O wide one, ever-vigilant; O Father Heaven, drive away misfortune from here.

sanskrit: ye no vacobhir uta daṃsanābhis tanvaṃ soma paritāpayante | nīcais tān vṛśca na yathā virukṣan mā te dṛśan sūryam uccarantam ||
english: Those who afflict our body with words and sorcerous acts, O Soma — cut them down low so that they may wither; may they not see the sun rising.

sanskrit: tvayeṣvā tvayā soma dhanvanā tvayā muṣṭighnā śāśadmahe vayam | tvaṃ tān vṛśca ya idaṃ na ?ādṛśākaren? hanāma daṇḍair uta daṃsanābhiḥ ||
english: With your arrows, O Soma, with your bow, with your fist-smiting power do we prevail. Cut down those who have done this wrong — we strike them with staffs and with mighty acts.

sanskrit: padena tān padanyo nayantu vadhair enān pitaro daṃsayantu | yathā na jīvāt katamaś canaiṣām ||
english: May the treader lead them by the footstep; may the ancestors teach them their doom with blows — so that not one of them may live.

sanskrit: yena somāditiḥ pathā mitrā vā yanty adruhaḥ | tenā no 'vitā bhuvaḥ ||
english: By the path by which Soma, Aditi, and the Mitras travel, the guileless ones — by that path be our protector.

sanskrit: yo naḥ soma suśaṃsino duḥśaṃso abhidāsati | vajreṇāsya mukhe jahi sa saṃpiṣṭo apāyati ||
english: He who harms us the well-praised, the ill-praiser, O Soma — strike him in the face with the vajra; crushed, he shall go away.

sanskrit: yo naḥ somābhidāsati sanābhir yaś ca niṣṭiyaḥ | apa tasya balaṃ tira mahīva dyaur vadha tmanā ||
english: He who attacks us, O Soma — both the kinsman and the outsider — cut off his strength; like great heaven, smite him with your own killing blow.

sanskrit: punar agham aghakṛtam etu devāḥ punar ena enaskṛtaṃ vijānat | punaḥ putraḥ pitaram etu vidvān hatām uta yad asya svam asti ||
english: O gods, may evil return upon the evil-doer; may guilt recognize him who made the guilt. May the knowing son return to strike the father — and whatever is his own is struck down too.

sanskrit: yena cāsau śapati yena cainaṃ śapāmasi | ubhau saṃvṛhya tau tasmād antikād dhetim asyatām ||
english: With what curse he curses, and with what curse we curse him in return — grasping both together, from that near place let them hurl the bolt at him.

sanskrit: ye pārthivāsaḥ śapathā ya urāv antarikṣe | ye vātasya prabharmaṇi tebhiṣ ṭaṃ vartayāmasi yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ vayaṃ dviṣmaḥ ||
english: The curses that dwell in the earth, those in the broad atmosphere, those in the wind's current — with all of these we roll him over: him who hates us, and him whom we hate.

sanskrit: ye asmān parisīsṛpuḥ kulīpayāni bibhrataḥ | ud devas teṣāṃ vṛścata mūlam urvārvo yathā ||
english: Those who have crept around us bearing harmful charms — may the god pluck out their root as one pulls up a cucumber vine.

sanskrit: yad devā aghadhā agham anyasminn ā sisaṃkṣati | bhāro aghasya duḥsahaḥ pratyak kartāram ṛcchatu ||
english: When the evil-placing gods seek to fasten evil upon another — the burden of that evil, hard to bear, shall come back upon its maker.

sanskrit: punar evāghadhām aghaṃ dyumnam ?ivaitur arṣatu | ādityāduryāmahiṣā? mahī sindhor ivāvaniḥ ||
english: Let the evil of the evil-placer flow back again, as glory flows; like the great flood of the river Sindhu, let it roll back upon them.

sanskrit: śaśvad didyut kriyamāṇā pratīcī ni hi paptat | pratyak kartāram ṛcchatu ||
english: The lightning bolt ever hurled, flying westward, has indeed fallen — may it come back and strike the one who sent it.

sanskrit: śaśvantam ic chāśadānam anyasmā iṣuṃ dihānam | pratīcī śarur ṛcchatu ||
english: The one who ever presses forward against another, smearing arrows with poison — let the arrow strike him back in return.

sanskrit: yad etad bhūri śāśadat pratīcīnam apohase | viṣād iva viṣam addhi tat ||
english: Whatever you hurl abundantly against the one facing you to drive him away — eat that as poison eats poison.

sanskrit: namas te pravato napād yatas tapaḥ samūhase | mṛḍā nas tanūbhyaś śaṃ nas tokebhyas kṛdhi ||
english: Homage to you, O Son of the slope, from where you gather heat — be gracious to our bodies; bring well-being to our offspring.

sanskrit: pravato napān namo astu tubhyaṃ namas te hetaye tapuṣyai | vidma te dhāma paramaṃ guhā yat samudre antar nihitāsi nābhiḥ ||
english: Homage to you, O Son of the slope; homage to your burning bolt. We know your highest abode in the hidden place — you are set within the ocean as the navel.

sanskrit: yāṃ tvā devā ajanayanta viśva iṣuṃ kṛṇvānā asanāya tṛṣvīm | sā no mṛḍa vidathe gṛṇānā mitrasya ca varuṇasya praśiṣṭau ||
english: You whom all the gods begot, fashioning you as an arrow, swift and fierce for casting — praised in our assembly, be gracious to us under the direction of Mitra and Varuṇa.

sanskrit: yūyaṃ naḥ pravato napān marutaḥ sūryatvacaḥ | śarma yacchātha saprathaḥ ||
english: O Maruts with sun-like skin, O Sons of the slope, grant us shelter, grant us wide protection.

sanskrit: mamṛḍatā suṣūdatā mṛḍā no aghnyābhyaḥ | tokāya tanve ca ||
english: Be gracious, be completely gracious — be gracious to us for the sake of our cows, our offspring, and our bodies.

sanskrit: namas te astu vidyute namas te stanayitnave | namas te astv aśmane yenā dūḍāśe asyasi ||
english: Homage to you, O lightning; homage to you, O thunder. Homage to you, O hailstone, with which you hurl against the steadfast one.

sanskrit: yo asmān brahmaṇaspate 'devo abhidāsati | sarvaṃ taṃ rīradhāsi naḥ ||
english: He who, being no god, attacks us — O Brahmaṇaspati, deliver all of him up to us.

sanskrit: yebhiḥ soma sāhantya- -asurān randhayāsai | tebhir no 'vitā bhuvaḥ ||
english: With those powers by which you, O Soma, overcome and subdue the asuras — with those same powers be our protector.

sanskrit: yāni devā asurāṇām ojāṃsy avṛṇīdhvam | tebhir no adhi vocata ||
english: The strengths of the asuras that you, O gods, have chosen for yourselves — with those same strengths speak on our behalf.

sanskrit: ud enam uttaraṃ naya- -agne ghṛtebhir āhutaḥ | sam enaṃ varcasā sṛja devānāṃ bhāgadhā asat ||
english: O Agni, fed with ghee, lead him upward, to the highest place; unite him with radiance — may he become a sharer in the gods' portion.

sanskrit: indremaṃ prataraṃ kṛdhi sajātānām asad vaśī | rāyaspoṣeṇa saṃ sṛja prajayā ca bahuṃ kṛdhi ||
english: O Indra, make him foremost among his kinsmen; may he be the master of his peers. Unite him with the abundance of wealth; make him great through offspring.

sanskrit: yasya kṛṇmo gṛhe havis tam agne vardhayā tvam | tasmai somo adhi bruvad ayaṃ ca brahmaṇaspatiḥ ||
english: He in whose house we make the oblation — him, O Agni, do you increase. May Soma speak on his behalf, and this Brahmaṇaspati too.
